text:
Jordan: FYI opened PR #8321 that changes the prefill scheduling heuristic and touches KV shard assignment. Short description: tries to reduce cold-prefill duplication by spreading prefill work across fewer workers. Needs quick perf sanity before merge.

Sana: Thanks — can you summarize benchmarks? Any p95 regressions on longseq?

Jordan: Ran local microbench + canary-like sim. Short results pasted below. Also CI perf-run attached (link in bot).

Jordan: ```
Benchmark  | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | RSS(MB)
before     | 12.4    | 34.9    | 4300
after      | 13.1    | 48.5    | 4680
delta p95  | +13.6ms (+39%)
delta rss  | +380MB (+8.8%)
```

Kevin: ugh p95 jump looks concerning. Is that from more contention during prefill windows?

Jordan: Yes looks like peak contention when multiple longseq requests trigger prefill at similar time. The heuristic reduces duplicate prefill but increases per-worker load spike. I added a mitigation flag to throttle prefill concurrency.

Matt: CI bot shows the perf-run with more representative traffic: ci-bot: perf-run summary -> p95 +18%, RSS +260MB. Link: https://ci.internal/perf/8321

Olga: Can you share the exact toggle and rollout plan? If we can canary at low % and auto-revert on p95 > +25% then this might be OK.

Jordan: Toggle is runtime flag: "prefill_shard_concurrency=2" (default 4). Rollout plan in PR description: canary 5% for 2 hours, then 20% for 4 hours, monitor p95 and RSS. Revert if p95 > +25% or OOMs.

Sana: Quick code question — PR touches scheduler::assign_shards(). Did you add a new lock? I saw a small critical section in the diff that might serialize assign work.

Jordan: Not a new global lock, just per-shard atomic. But the code path can cause more async tasks to pile up per worker. I'm happy to refactor if folks prefer spreading tasks across time slices.

Kevin: My quick suggestion: add jitter to prefill start times and keep concurrency at 3 instead of 2. That should smooth the p95 without reintroducing duplicate work. Can you benchmark that variant?

Jordan: Will run a microbench with concurrency=3 + jitter and post numbers in ~40m.

Matt: From an ops POV, if we proceed we want: 1) canary policy described in PR, 2) dashboard with per-worker queue depth and RSS, 3) alert rule for p95 delta. I can stash dashboard tiles.

Olga: +1 on dashboard. Also request at least one more LGTM from infra side (Kevin or Sana).

Jordan: Ping @Sana @Kevin — would you be able to give a quick review and LGTM if the concurrency=3+jitter numbers look ok?

Sana: I'll take a look later today. If the p95 is < +20% and RSS < +300MB I'll approve.

Kevin: Same. If Jordan posts the new numbers I'll do a focused review.

ci-bot: Build #8321: perf-run finished. Artifacts: https://ci.internal/artifacts/8321/perf.txt.

Jordan: Uploaded new run (concurrency=3 + jitter=uniform(0,50ms)). Results: ```
Benchmark  | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | RSS(MB)
before     | 12.4    | 34.9    | 4300
after (c=3) | 12.8   | 41.6    | 4450
delta p95  | +6.7ms (+19%)
delta rss  | +150MB (+3.5%)
```

Matt: That looks reasonable to me. Still want the dashboard and canary gating.

Sana: Numbers look ok to me too. I'll give LGTM on the PR assuming we ship the concurrency=3+jitter variant and follow the rollout plan + alerting.

Kevin: LGTM as well. Please include the perf artifacts link in the PR description and schedule canary tonight 6-8pm PT.

Jordan: Added artifacts and updated rollout plan in PR. Scheduling canary 18:00-20:00 PT. Thanks all.

Olga: Thanks — will standby for rollback if alerts fire. :thumbsup:

Jordan: Closing loop: will merge after 1hr quiet and then kick off canary. If no objections I'll merge at 17:10 PT.

Sana: No objections from me.

Kevin: 👍

Jordan: Merged and canary started. Monitoring dashboard link: https://dash.internal/c/8321. Revert plan ready.

ci-bot: Deploy event: merged PR #8321 by Jordan. Canary rollout started at 1698745860.

Olga: Keeping watch, will update if we see anomalies.

Jordan: Thanks team!"
